title: Aurek Network — DM EYES ONLY
summary: **Not a faction the party knows exists. The hidden network Vaeloran runs under the alias Aurek Voln Drowhiss — an anagram of his own name.**
html:
Aurek Network — DM EYES ONLY

Not a faction the party knows exists. The hidden network Vaeloran runs under the alias Aurek Voln Drowhiss — an anagram of his own name.

What It Is

A loose, deniable network of operatives and assets used to engineer instability. Vaeloran does not have employees in the conventional sense. He has people who believe they serve other patrons or other gods.

Components

  • Naturus Cult / Kaelith — believes she serves Naturus.
  • Guilded Veil / Merric — believes he serves the city’s balance.
  • The Coin Cipher — Vaeloran’s primary courier network for sensitive cargo. Founded 20 years ago through an intermediary. Even the Cipher’s Mint doesn’t know who founded them — they believe they serve a wealthy anonymous patron.
  • Compromised council assistants (e.g. Dara Voss’s assistant on the Veil’s payroll).
  • Compromised Aelorian moneylenders (e.g. Davos Hark in Aeloria — lightly leveraged via Aurek shell creditors).
  • Ciphered correspondence sent through dead drops, carried by Coin Cipher couriers who don’t know who they serve.

How the Network Operates

  • Crises are caused or allowed.
  • Aurek’s “advice” appears to solve them.
  • Council becomes increasingly dependent on Vaeloran’s foresight.
  • Each segment of the network believes they’re independent. Vaeloran’s signature trick — compartmentalisation.

What Will Break It

  • The anagram reveal (see Main Plot - Vaeloran Conspiracy).
  • Merric’s break point — if he tells Orin everything.
  • Kaelith captured and interrogated.
  • A Coin Cipher Carrier captured — drop points and broker contacts surface.
  • A Coin Cipher Broker compromised — Mint locations surface.
  • The Mint itself rolled up — ledgers show all “Patron” payments come through a single ciphered account, traceable to Vaeloran.
  • Taren Myles turning against Vaeloran.

Redundancy

Vaeloran’s compartmentalisation means no single thread cracking the conspiracy. The party will need to dismantle multiple arms separately:

  • Stop Kaelith → Naturus pressure ends in the territories.
  • Break Merric → the Guilded Veil’s role in destabilisation ends.
  • Expose the Coin Cipher → logistics shatter; he can’t move components or letters safely.
  • Each is a separate session-arc payoff.

Cross-references

  • NPC: Vaeloran Duskwhisper
  • Plot: Main Plot - Vaeloran Conspiracy · Vaeloran Lich Progress · Instability Clock
  • Factions: Naturus Cult · Guilded Veil · The Coin Cipher

title: Aurum Dominion
summary: **The most organised external threat in the campaign — three simultaneous agendas.**
html:
The Aurum Dominion
Type Centralised Monarchy with Bureaucracy
Ruler Emperor Valerius Kaelthorn
Capital Auranova
Religion Thalasia (state) + Aetherius. Suppresses Luminos worship.

The most organised external threat in the campaign — three simultaneous agendas.

Three Active Agendas

1. Trade Dominance (immediate)

Dominion envoys are in Aeloria pushing exclusive trade contracts with Ironhold’s master smiths. Guildmaster Bryndis Ashveil refuses; younger smith Corvan Drake wants the deal. If Drake wins the political battle inside Ironhold, the Dominion gains military production leverage over the southern Aelorian Territories.

2. Valdris Search (ongoing)

Aurum Sentinels quietly excavating beneath the Aurora Peaks searching for Valdris’s sanctum. The Dominion has protected Valdris’s phylactery location for 300 years in exchange for arcane consultation. They now believe Valdris may be moving (through Sylas) and want to understand what that means — or exploit it.

3. Military Build-up (simmering)

Crown Prince Aurek leading military exercises near the Aelorian border. Framed as “defensive readiness.” Princess Selene running intelligence operations through Lady Selendra Kaelthorn’s network. Long-term goal: eventual annexation of the Aelorian Territories if their independence can be sufficiently undermined.

Intelligence Operations

Princess Selene (22) is the most dangerous actor in the Dominion — more than her brother. She has a personal spy network operating in Aeloria. Lady Selendra Kaelthorn runs it. They are aware of Vaeloran but have not identified him as “Aurek” and are not set up to connect the two names on their own — they think he is simply a powerful independent mage worth cultivating or neutralising. (No scheduled reveal. Only the party can bridge those identities, or a dramatic in-game event may force it into Selene’s file.)

The Aurum Sentinels

Protection force of the Dominion. Disciplined, skilled in crystal-based magic and advanced combat. Both military force and symbol of Dominion authority. Three scouts were on the north road outside Aeloria the night Matilda disappeared.

meta.status: active — Aurum weapons contract vote at end of Session 7

html:
The Forge Council of Ironhold

Ironhold’s local governing body. Nine seats: seven forge-guild masters + two civic delegates appointed by the merchant class. Simple majority of the full nine (5+) is needed to pass any motion — ties or shortfalls default to status quo. The Council currently sits on a knife-edge over the Aurum Dominion weapons contract. Current standing: 5 pro-Aurum, 3 anti, 1 undecided. Vote scheduled for the closing scene of Session 7.

Structure

  • Nine seats. Seven guild masters (one per forge guild) + two civic delegates appointed by Ironhold’s merchant class.
  • Simple majority of the full nine (5+) required to pass any motion. Abstentions count as neither for nor against but do NOT lower the majority threshold — so an abstention on the pro side is functionally the same as a vote against.
  • Meets every eighth day in the great domed hall at the centre of the Council Ward. Extraordinary sessions can be called by any four members with 24 hours’ notice.
  • Chair rotates annually. Current chair: Bryndis Ashveil (senior of the active guildmasters). Chair controls the order of business, calls votes, but has no additional vote or tiebreaker — Ironhold prefers deadlock to imposed decisions.
  • Reports upward to the Aelorian Council on trade and defence matters via Vorik Stonestrong (Ironhold’s dwarven envoy resident in Aeloria; has not visited Ironhold in six years).
  • Stonecut Ward has no direct seat — its dwarven population speaks to the Council through the Precision Guildmaster (currently Gundri Stonebreath) and, informally, through the Stonecut elder-advocate Torvi.

The nine seats — current state

Firm pro-Aurum (4 votes)

  • Master Corvan Drake — Ingots Guild. Firm pro. The engine of the Aurum push. Sees the contract triple the volume of his forge, sees the strings as negotiable in practice. Has been actively courting the undecided and the soft. See Corvan Drake.
  • Master Ren Vestic — Armours Guild. Firm pro. Mid-40s, human, pragmatic-not-cruel. The most principled of the pro-Aurum three: he votes with Drake because Aurum’s terms genuinely double his guild’s income and he thinks Bryndis’s fears are old-woman politics. He is the most likely of Drake’s block to flip if presented with clean public evidence of Drake’s Kellan framing. He does not think of himself as compromised and dislikes being taken for granted.
  • Master Rell Tavish — Mail Guild. Firm pro. Human, late-50s, comfortable, deferential to Drake. Weakest of the pro-Aurum three — votes with Drake because Drake is loud and he doesn’t want a fight. Corruptible with less effort than Osgood, but nobody has bothered yet because his vote comes free with Drake’s.
  • Master Brannic Wold — Fittings Guild. Firm pro. Half-dwarf, early-50s, blunt. Votes gold-now-over-principles-later on any given day. Not principled enough to flip on principle, not politically important enough to be a target. Filler vote for the pro block.

Soft pro-Aurum, bribable (1 vote)

  • Councillor Osgood — Merchants’ Civic Seat. Currently pro because Drake has been buying his suppers for three weeks. Tired, aging, not enthusiastic. The abstention lever: if presented with evidence of Drake’s gifts and the ethics-committee angle, he will abstain rather than fight. Will not vote anti — he is too tired for a fight — but abstaining is enough.

Firm anti-Aurum (3 votes)

  • Master Bryndis Ashveil — Blades Guild. Firm anti. Council chair this year. Sees Aurum’s terms as a strategic surrender wearing a merchant’s coat. “They will not need to conquer us. They will need only to change their minds.” Will not compromise. Coordinating the anti-Aurum bloc.
  • Master Gundri Stonebreath — Precision Guild. Firm anti. Dwarf male, ~140 years old, quiet, deeply competent. Speaks for the Stonecut Ward’s precision-work masters — jewellery, mechanical fittings, dwarven-fine forgework. Sees Aurum’s bulk-blade demand as a death sentence for boutique dwarven craft (contract volumes leave no capacity for the small work). Torvi’s ally. Would sooner break the Council than vote pro.
  • Master Vaelin Rook — Ornaments Guild. Firm anti. Half-elf, artist-turned-guildmaster, late-30s. Sees the contract as annihilation of ornamental and ceremonial work — Aurum wants blades and mail, not filigree. Votes with Bryndis on principle and interest simultaneously. Personally close to Bryndis’s protégée Ana Kest.

Undecided (1 vote)

  • Councillor Merla Vinn — Merchants’ Civic Seat. Human female, mid-40s, cordage-and-canvas merchant, sharp, cautious. She has not been bought, hasn’t taken Drake’s meetings, has read the Aurum terms herself. She is weighing them honestly. She is the party’s persuade-target. Levers that move her toward anti: (a) any evidence that Drake’s evidence against Kellan is manufactured; (b) any credible reading that the Aurum terms disadvantage Ironhold’s smaller guilds long-term; (c) any endorsement from Torvi via Gundri. Levers that push her toward pro: (a) a genuinely generous Aurum concession offered before the vote; (b) Bryndis being seen to overreach or grandstand. Currently reading the vote at 50/50.

Vote math — pathways to defeat the contract

The motion needs 5 votes to pass. Anything less fails and defaults to status quo (no contract).

Baseline (nothing changes): - Pro: Drake, Vestic, Tavish, Wold, Osgood = 5. Undecided goes pro (Drake pressures her hard the day before) or anti (marginal). Motion passes 5–3 or 5–4.

Party pathway A — Osgood abstains + Merla Vinn goes anti. Present Osgood with evidence of Drake’s gifts + the ethics-committee angle. He abstains. Simultaneously give Merla clean anti-arguments (Aurum terms analysis or Kellan framing exposure). - Result: 4 pro (Drake, Vestic, Tavish, Wold), 4 anti (Bryndis, Gundri, Rook, Vinn), 1 abstain (Osgood). Motion fails.

Party pathway B — flip Vestic to abstain via public Kellan-framing reveal. Expose Drake’s Kellan framing at the Council session itself. Vestic — principled and dislikes being played — abstains in protest. - Result: 4 pro (Drake, Tavish, Wold, Osgood), 3 anti, 1 abstain (Vestic), 1 undecided. Then whichever way Vinn breaks: at worst 5–3 (motion still fails because pro sits at 4 from firm block + Osgood). Wait — Vestic abstaining leaves Drake with Tavish, Wold, Osgood = 4 pro. Even if Vinn goes pro, that’s 5 → passes. So pathway B requires Osgood ALSO abstain, OR Vinn go anti.

Party pathway C — combine A and B. Expose Drake’s Kellan framing AND deploy the Osgood evidence. Vestic + Osgood both abstain. Vinn breaks anti after seeing the framing reveal. - Result: 3 pro (Drake, Tavish, Wold), 4 anti (Bryndis, Gundri, Rook, Vinn), 2 abstain (Vestic, Osgood). Motion fails decisively 4–3. This is the definitive win path.

Party pathway D — turn Bram against Drake for a Foundry Row testimony. Bram (Drake’s Furnace apprentice) has evidence of Drake’s operational shortcuts that endanger workers. If Bram testifies at Council, Wold (Fittings) — who has a soft spot for foundry workers — may flip to abstain. Combined with any of A/B, this widens the failure margin.

What the party cannot easily do: - Flip Drake (his interest is his forge tripling; no lever short of assassination moves him). - Flip Tavish outright (he votes with the loudest voice in the room; even flipping him only works if Drake is publicly humiliated first). - Flip Wold outright (see above; only Bram-testimony route). - Turn Gundri, Rook, or Bryndis pro (they are unmovable and the party wouldn’t want to anyway).

Party lever mapping (quick reference)

Seat Vote Lever Where the lever comes from
Drake Firm pro (no viable lever) —
Vestic (Armours) Firm pro Public Kellan-framing exposure Kellan documents + Mara Volk (50gp each) + Vasso
Tavish (Mail) Firm pro Needs Drake humiliated first Chain from Vestic route
Wold (Fittings) Firm pro Bram testimony on foundry safety Broken Anvil, late evening
Osgood (Civic) Soft pro Ethics-committee warning re: Drake’s gifts Party gathers evidence of Drake’s supper-and-box hospitality; delivered privately
Bryndis (Blades) Firm anti — Already anti; ally
Gundri (Precision) Firm anti — Ally; reached via Torvi
Rook (Ornaments) Firm anti — Ally; endorsement from Bryndis
Vinn (Civic) Undecided Aurum-terms analysis + Kellan reveal + Torvi endorsement Reading the contract + framing exposure + Stonecut backing

Meeting procedure and the Aurum vote

  • Vote day: end of Session 7 (as per Arc 02 plan). Extraordinary session convened for this purpose.
  • Order of business: 1. Chair (Bryndis) reads the motion aloud. 2. Proposer (Drake) speaks for. 3. Chair or nominee speaks against (Bryndis). 4. Open floor — any councillor may speak (this is where public reveals land; Kellan-framing exposure lives here). 5. Envoy Veris permitted to make a brief statement (traditional courtesy). 6. Vote called seat-by-seat, chair last.
  • Envoy Veris will be present in the chamber’s observer gallery. His conduct if the motion fails: polite disappointment, an unreadable expression, private words with Drake afterward. He does not blame the Council. He blames the party if he clocks their involvement — which he will if they’re prominent in the floor debate.

What the Council doesn’t know

  • Kellan Bracewell is Guilded Veil and was framed by Drake.
  • The Aurum Dominion’s long-term plan is dependency, not partnership.
  • Vaeloran Duskwhisper exists as a hostile force. Council believes Aeloria’s civic power sits with the visible Aeloria Council.
  • The Coin Cipher chest, Wesley Halloran, the Vroth-Khorn Seal — none of it is on their radar.

What individual members know that others don’t

  • Bryndis: suspects (correctly) that Kellan was framed. Cannot prove it. Has not shared this suspicion at Council.
  • Gundri: knows Stonecut sentiment on the contract is united anti. Has told Bryndis. Has not told the pro-block.
  • Drake: knows he has 5–3 with Osgood, needs the vote called before anyone lands a blow.
  • Vestic: does not know Drake framed Kellan. If he learns this at Council, he will react publicly.
  • Osgood: knows he took the coin box. Has not opened it. Tells himself he hasn’t decided.
  • Vinn: knows she hasn’t decided. Is genuinely reading the contract. Will be moved by evidence, not appeals.

Cross-references

  • Location: Ironhold · The Heart of Ironhold (kept in the reliquary chamber beneath the Council Hall’s central dome)
  • NPCs — pro bloc: Corvan Drake · Councillor Osgood · Master Ren Vestic (stub pending) · Master Rell Tavish (stub pending) · Master Brannic Wold (stub pending)
  • NPCs — anti bloc: Bryndis Ashveil · Master Gundri Stonebreath (stub pending) · Master Vaelin Rook (stub pending)
  • NPC — undecided: Councillor Merla Vinn (stub pending)
  • Adjacent: Torvi (Stonecut advocate — Gundri’s ally) · Ana Kest (Bryndis’s protégée, Rook’s friend) · Bram (Wold-lever route) · Kellan Bracewell (framing evidence source) · Mara Volk (sells framing documents 50gp each) · Envoy Veris Caelthorn (observer in chamber)
  • Factions: Aurum Dominion · Guilded Veil
  • Sessions: Session 07 - Ironhold and the Forge Council

title: Lethraliri (Ancient — Extinct)
summary: **Second Age civilisation that thrived in the Frostwood Marsh. Skilled in ice and water magic. Now extinct as a civilisation — but two threads survive: the fenling carry fragments of the culture; the Six Wardens carry the seal.**

meta.status: extinct as a living civilisation — a fragment remains as the [[Lore and Legends/The Fenling|fenling]] and as the [[Lore and Legends/The Six Wardens|Six Wardens]]

html:
Lethraliri (Ancient — Extinct)

Second Age civilisation that thrived in the Frostwood Marsh. Skilled in ice and water magic. Now extinct as a civilisation — but two threads survive: the fenling carry fragments of the culture; the Six Wardens carry the seal.

Built stilt settlements with translucent ice sculptures and bioluminescent flora. At the end of the Second Age they were called on to help seal Vroth-Khorn beneath the marsh — and their civilisation ended in that act.

What they left behind

  • The Frozen Spire and the ruins beneath the marsh. Physically intact. The Spire is the keystone of the seal on Vroth-Khorn. The frozen Lethraliri scholars inside form the volume of the seal.
  • The Six Wardens. Six Lethraliri elders who did not enter the freeze — instead took living or half-living forms at cardinal points around the marsh to anchor the shape of the binding. Four still function; one is destroyed, one is corrupted. See The Six Wardens for the full roster and current state. Tracked live on the Seal Clock.
  • The fenling. Once dozens of small villages ringed the marsh; today one remains — Coldhearth — carrying fragmentary Lethraliri words, rituals, and songs handed down without their meaning. See The Fenling.

Significance

The ruins contain knowledge of the shard energies in the marsh. The Frozen Spire (their magical research centre) may contain information about the meteor shards that Vaeloran has not yet found — and, more importantly, the ice-script that names Vroth-Khorn and holds the ritual formulae of the binding.

Any surviving Lethraliri knowledge is dangerous to recover: pronouncing Vroth-Khorn’s true name aloud weakens the seal incrementally.

title: Naturus Cult
summary: Rot and decay are natural processes that bring renewal. The world must be broken down to be reborn. The Divine Gate should be weakened to allow Naturus's influence back into the material plane more directly.
html:
The Naturus Cult
Type Underground religious / terror organisation
Nominal leader Sister Kaelith
True patron Naturus (Betrayer God) — through whispers and manipulation
Connection Part of Vaeloran’s engineered instability network — though Kaelith doesn’t know this

What They Believe

Rot and decay are natural processes that bring renewal. The world must be broken down to be reborn. The Divine Gate should be weakened to allow Naturus’s influence back into the material plane more directly.

What They’re Actually Doing

  • Creating engineered unrest that feeds Vaeloran’s Instability Clock.
  • Corrupting the farmlands and woods around Aeloria — the southeastern farmlands (gnoll attacks), the brook at Stillbrook on the southern road, scattered woodland patches.
  • Using Guilded Veil tunnel infrastructure beneath Aeloria for meetings.
  • Charming and controlling creatures (the gnoll pack leader; the deal with Vrass for caravan ambush) to create visible threats.
  • Establishing small shrines to Naturus in remote locations across the Aelorian Territories.

Current Operations

  • Centred in the Aelorian Territories. Kaelith moves between woods, abandoned farmhouses, and the Pig’s Head tunnels. Hard to pin down.
  • Naturus graffiti appearing on Temple of Luminos walls in Aeloria (Kaelith’s operatives).
  • Has made a deal with Vrass (young black dragon, displaced from the Frostwood Marsh) to thin caravans on the southern road.
  • Has not yet pushed corruption beyond the Aelorian Territories. Future arcs will see her expand westward (Verdant Expanse), northwest (Stonemarked passes), or further south (Ironhold roads). DM’s call when ready.

The “K” Note

A note signed “K” (Sister Kaelith) grants access to the Pig’s Head Inn back rooms without Gerald’s screening. The party found reference to this in the gnoll den writings. Using the note flags the holder to Merric immediately. See The K Note.

html:
Order of the Silver Crescent
Type Monastic / martial order
Deity Lunara (the Moonwalker)
Base Lunara Monastery, Aurora Peaks
Alignment Guardians of celestial balance

Structure (Ascending)

  1. Initiates (Aspirants) — entry level, fundamental teachings, gemstone connection beginning.
  2. Novices (Duskwalkers) — apprentices to Enlightened Guardians, learn fine jewellery and celestial craft.
  3. Silver Crescent Instructors (Sensei) — experienced monks, train Initiates and Novices.
  4. Enlightened Guardians (Dawnbringers) — scholars and protectors, preserve ancient wisdom, lead ceremonies.
  5. Gemstone Keepers — profound connection to the gemstone collection, mentors for meditation.
  6. Lunar Elders (High Masters) — highest rank, guide the monastery, teach the Silver Crescent Dance.

The Silver Crescent Dance

The order’s signature martial arts technique. Combines graceful movements with precise strikes. Monks emulate the path of the moon in combat — moving with fluidity and grace, mimicking the celestial body’s cycle from crescent to full.

Path of the Silver Crescent Dancer (Monk Subclass)

Homebrew subclass — full features in Path of the Silver Crescent Dancer (monk subclass).

  • Lunar Stance (3rd): Increased movement speed and advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics).
  • Radiant Strikes (6th): While in Lunar Stance, unarmed strikes deal +1d4 radiant damage.
  • Lunar Radiance (11th): Shed dim light; allies within gain temp HP = WIS modifier; advantage on WIS saves vs frightened/charmed.
  • Eclipse Form (17th): Resistance to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing; +1d6 radiant to unarmed strikes.

Lore

Founded during the Second Age during celestial upheaval. Played a pivotal role in Eldoria’s restoration after the Usurpation. Gemstones are sacred — each monk forms a bond with a specific stone for meditation.

Cross-references

  • Pantheon: Pantheon of Eldoria (Lunara)
  • Location: _Aurum Dominion Overview (Lunara Monastery)

title: Sylvarian Enclaves
summary: **Naturus corruption (Sister Kaelith's operations) spreading into the forest edges.** Sacred groves near Silentwood darkening. The old elf puritan faction sees it as punishment for allowing non-elves in. The multicultural faction looks desperately for an external cause.
html:
Sylvarian Enclaves
Type Network of elven settlements in the Verdant Expanse
Government Mix of elected/appointed civic officials and druidic councils
Culture Emphasis on art, magic, and diplomacy. Decisions by consensus. Originally elf-only; now multicultural though some hold to old ways.

Major Settlements

  • Eldralor — built on the Eldorian Tree (largest tree in Verdant Expanse). Council of Elders. Cultural heart.
  • Celestia Glade — floating island. Levitation crystals. Mystical gardens. Rises during celestial events.
  • Silentwood — secretive, skilled assassins, shadow guardians.
  • Aurelia Haven — river settlement, arts and trade hub.

Current Situation

Naturus corruption (Sister Kaelith’s operations) spreading into the forest edges. Sacred groves near Silentwood darkening. The old elf puritan faction sees it as punishment for allowing non-elves in. The multicultural faction looks desperately for an external cause.

Countdown: 3 sessions ignored → Enclaves send emissary to Aeloria.

title: The Coin Cipher
summary: **A specialised criminal courier network in the Aelorian underworld. Moves high-value, sensitive cargo with absolute discretion. Their hidden Patron is Vaeloran — no member knows.**
html:
The Coin Cipher

A specialised criminal courier network in the Aelorian underworld. Moves high-value, sensitive cargo with absolute discretion. Their hidden Patron is Vaeloran — no member knows.

What they do

Transport and laundering of high-value, sensitive cargo. Goods other criminals won’t touch — magical components, sealed correspondence, contraband too rare or too dangerous to move openly. “If you can pay, we can move it. We don’t ask what’s in the box.”

Structure

The Mint — the inner ring. About ten people. Coordinates all operations.

Carriers — courier-level operatives. Move sealed packages between drops. Wear a small tattoo of a coin behind the right ear. Don’t know what they carry. Maybe forty in total across Eldoria.

Brokers — middlemen. Take orders from clients, set prices, never touch goods. Maybe a dozen.

The Forge — sealed-document and ward specialists. Make the wax seals, the magical wards on chests, the cipher-keys. Very small group, maybe four.

The Edge — violence specialists. Used rarely. When the Coin Cipher retaliates, the Edge does it. Maybe six.

The eclipse mark

A stylised eclipse — a sun half-eaten by shadow. Used on seals, on chest banding, occasionally as a tattoo. Means: “This is Coin Cipher cargo. Interfere at your peril.”

Public reputation

Among criminals: respected, feared, paid well, retaliate harder. Other criminal groups don’t poach Coin Cipher business; doing so is suicide. The Guilded Veil cooperates with them sometimes but doesn’t try to absorb them.

Among honest folk: largely unknown. The Coin Cipher doesn’t market itself.

Relationship with the Guilded Veil

Independent specialist, professionally tolerated, occasionally subcontracted. Different markets, different scale. They don’t compete.

  • The Veil makes its money off thousands of small transactions and street control.
  • The Cipher makes its money off a handful of enormous ones.

The Veil tolerates them because: (a) wiping them out would cost more than it earns — the Edge retaliates hard, (b) they don’t compete for Veil revenue, (c) the Veil sometimes pays them for jobs the Veil can’t safely run itself.

The Cipher tolerates the Veil because: (a) avoiding pointless wars is good business, (b) the Veil’s tunnel network sometimes makes courier routes easier (the Cipher pays the Veil quietly for access), (c) sharing Aeloria with a much larger criminal organisation means trouble comes for the Veil first.

Information flow between them is almost zero. Two parallel ecosystems.

What Torren knows

He’s encountered the eclipse symbol perhaps two or three times in his Assassin career. He knows: - The seal means “do not interfere” — strongly. - The carriers wear coin-tattoos behind the ear. - Crossing them is dangerous. - He’s heard a rumour, dismissed as criminal mythology, that the Coin Cipher has a “Patron” no one has ever met. (The rumour is true. The Patron is Vaeloran. Torren has not connected this and won’t, naturally, for a long time.)

DM secrets — Vaeloran’s reach

The Coin Cipher is Vaeloran’s primary courier network for sensitive cargo. He founded it twenty years ago through an intermediary. Even the Mint doesn’t know who founded them. They believe they serve a wealthy, anonymous patron who pays in gold and silence.

What they’ve moved for him over the years: - Phylactery components (including the obsidian shard now on the party’s caravan). - Aurek correspondence between Vaeloran and his far-flung assets. - Modify-memory reagents and other lich-ritual components. - Sensitive intelligence packages between Vaeloran and members of the Aeloria Council whom he’s leveraged.

If exposed and rolled up, this would shatter a major arm of Vaeloran’s logistical operations. A late-campaign payoff.

Merric’s blind spot (the cosmic irony)

Merric (as Veilmaster of the Guilded Veil) has hired the Coin Cipher once or twice over the years for jobs the Veil couldn’t safely do itself. He paid them well; got clean delivery; asked no questions. He has no idea his own patron (the “Aurek Voln Drowhiss” alias he serves) is also the Cipher’s hidden Patron — and he is not set up to connect that on his own. No clock, no scheduled reveal. If he ever learns it (party choice or dramatic in-game trigger), the realisation hits him hard — he was paying the same hand twice over. See Merric’s file for reaction paths.

How to expose the Coin Cipher

Possible paths the campaign could take:

  • Capture a Carrier. Carriers don’t know the Patron, but interrogation surfaces drop points, broker contacts, and (if pressed) Mint locations.
  • Compromise a Broker. Brokers know the Mint’s coordination protocols, payment routes, and (importantly) the Patron’s cipher-style.
  • Find the Mint. Located in a hidden Aeloria back-room (not yet detailed). Rolling up the Mint surfaces ledgers — the ledgers would show that all “Patron” payments come through a single ciphered account, traceable with effort to Vaeloran.
  • The chest’s letter — if the party keeps the Coin Cipher correspondence from the chest, it will eventually match writing samples from Vaeloran’s tower (when the party finds the Aurek correspondence there).

Current Coin Cipher operations relevant to the party

  • The chest on the party’s caravan (delivered to Ironhold warehouse #14, picked up by a hooded courier, transported north in a small black carriage).
  • Several other parallel deliveries the party isn’t yet aware of, including modify-memory reagents being staged for Vaeloran’s Stage 4.

Cross-references

  • NPC: Vaeloran Duskwhisper · Merric Underbough · Torren
  • Faction: Aurek Network · Guilded Veil
  • Item: The Coin Cipher Chest
  • Plot: Main Plot - Vaeloran Conspiracy · Caravan to Ironhold

title: The Guilded Veil
summary: **A continent-adjacent thieves' network organised as six territorial cells across the Aelorian Territories, coordinated by a single hidden figure — **The Gilded** — whose identity is known only to the six Territorial Veilmasters.**

meta.status: active — six territorial cells + hidden coordinating head

html:
The Guilded Veil

A continent-adjacent thieves’ network organised as six territorial cells across the Aelorian Territories, coordinated by a single hidden figure — The Gilded — whose identity is known only to the six Territorial Veilmasters.

Structure

Three tiers.

1. The Gilded. Sits at the top. Wears a physical gilded veil — a gold-inlaid ceremonial mask that covers the entire face — at every appearance. Voice altered, gait deliberately unremarkable. Identity known only to the six Territorial Veilmasters, and even they know only that someone has held the veil for the last ten years; whether it has always been the same person, whether it is one of them, whether it is a group taking turns — nobody outside The Gilded is certain. See section below.

2. Six Territorial Veilmasters. Each runs a cell in one of the Veil’s six territorial holdings across the Aelorian Territories. Each reports to The Gilded via sending stone (see below). Quarterly they meet in person at a rotating location (most recently Kolt’s Depot). Each Veilmaster runs their territory autonomously — hiring, firing, wet-work decisions, tribute collection, tunnel infrastructure. The Gilded coordinates cross-territory business and adjudicates disputes.

3. Captains and operatives. Each Territorial Veilmaster runs their cell as they see fit. The Aeloria cell (the largest) is organised under six captains, each with a sector specialty. Smaller cells have simpler structures.

The Six Territorial Veilmasters

1. Aeloria Crossroads — Merric Underbough (“Rulden Marr”)

~40 operatives across six captains and their networks. The largest cell by an order of magnitude. Operates from the back rooms of the Pig’s Head Inn in the Ashgate Slums, via extensive tunnel infrastructure under the city. Merric is calm, calculating, and commands loyalty through competence rather than fear. He is Orin’s adoptive father — a fact he considers separate from his position.

Captains (roster):

  • Groodmet — “The Ledger” — finance, extortion.
  • Ambimar — “The Whisper” — espionage, intelligence.
  • Kargan Voss — “The Hammer” — enforcement, wet-work.
  • Selra “Quickfingers” — “The Hand” — theft, infiltration.
  • Varro Kain — “The Shade” — smuggling.
  • Edrin Vale — “The Quill” — forgery. Cover: The Gilded Quill.

Full roster and details: Guilded Veil Captains.

2. Ironhold — Kellan Bracewell

~20 operatives. Contract-adjacent smuggling, modest merchant tribute, occasional wet-work. Operates from Rustpocket — tunnel-network beneath the tenement blocks, safehouses run through friendly landladies. The cell keeps deliberate distance from Warehouse #14 (Coin Cipher territory); the two networks share the underground tunnel infrastructure but never each other’s business. Currently in hiding after Drake framed her — see her file for the full arc. Reports to The Gilded via sending stone.

3. Stonegate — Wenzel “The Kite” Tosscobble

~12 operatives. Halfling in her 60s, has run the Stonegate cell for twenty years. Focus: north-south smuggling through the Stonegate pass, small-scale merchant tribute in the lower town, occasional wet-work. Recruited Torren after his Watch discharge; sent him south to Aeloria roughly two years ago as an inter-cell liaison. Still considers him hers.

4. Duskmere — Berine Vosk

~15 operatives. Duskmere is a mid-sized coastal fishing and trade town on the eastern Aelorian coast, three days’ ride from Aeloria via the eastern road. Its cell focuses on maritime smuggling — goods that come in on foreign hulls the Watch cannot inspect politely — and on gathering intelligence from ship crews about affairs across the sea. Berine is human, mid-60s, ex-navy captain who took his pension and immediately went crooked. Runs his cell like a ship: written orders, chain of command, disciplinary flogging for infractions. Not warm. Not sentimental. Effective. Reports to The Gilded via sending stone.

5. Silverbrook — Idris Fenn

~8 operatives. Silverbrook is an agricultural region in the western Aelorian Territories — small farming villages arranged along a shallow river. Not a city; the cell is dispersed. Idris is halfling, mid-50s, formerly a merchant’s factor who quietly turned to running grain-tax evasion for the farming families that needed it. The cell’s work is quiet contract-fixing — smoothing over disputes, adjusting the paperwork on livestock deals, helping small farmers slip below Aelorian tax thresholds without formally cheating. Almost no wet-work. Almost no infrastructure. Runs on relationships. Reports to The Gilded via sending stone.

6. The Southern Road — Mesha “The Rider” Threll

~10 operatives, mostly mobile. Not based in a single settlement. Mesha’s cell covers the Aelorian southern trade route — the road between Aeloria, Kolt’s Depot, Stillbrook, and Ironhold — and works from a rotating network of safehouses along it. Focus: caravan-route intelligence (which the cell sells discreetly to Aeloria and Ironhold both), small-scale roadside protection racketing (kept modest — the Watch tolerates it as long as bodies don’t turn up), and inter-cell courier work when Veilmasters need messages moved fast. Mesha is a half-elf in her 40s, ex-caravan guard, spends more time on a horse than under a roof. Kolt is not Veil, but he and Mesha have a working understanding that neither of them names. Reports to The Gilded via sending stone.

The Gilded

The hidden coordinating head of the entire network. Sits at the top. Known to the six Veilmasters, unknown to everyone else.

Physical presence. At the quarterly meetings, The Gilded arrives already seated, wearing the ceremonial gold-inlaid mask that covers the entire face. Cloak covering the body. Voice altered — possibly magically. Never speaks in casual conversation; every sentence is measured. Sits, delivers decisions, listens to reports, leaves before the Veilmasters. Nobody knows how The Gilded arrives or departs.

Authority. Absolute on cross-territory business. Ignored, sometimes, on within-territory matters (Wenzel in particular runs Stonegate as if The Gilded barely exists).

History. The Guilded Veil had a known chief Veilmaster before The Gilded — an old thief who called himself simply The Chair (real name Elran Bosk, not that many of the Veilmasters ever heard it). The Chair sat in Aeloria; Merric served as his second. Ten years ago The Chair was reported killed — throat cut in a Silverbrook back alley, body recovered and identified. The six Territorial Veilmasters (including a younger Merric and a younger Wenzel) gathered in secret to decide the network’s future. When they gathered a second time three months later, The Gilded was present — mask, cloak, altered voice. The Gilded said only: “the network continues.” The Veilmasters voted to accept. Since then, quarterly meetings have been The Gilded’s forum.

What the Veilmasters privately suspect. No two agree.

  • Merric thinks The Gilded is The Chair — that Elran Bosk faked his own death and returned in anonymous form to remove himself from personal targeting.
  • Wenzel thinks The Gilded is “someone we all know,” meaning one of the six Territorial Veilmasters. She has not accused anyone.
  • Berine thinks The Gilded is a rotating role held by a small circle who takes the mask in turn. He is wrong.
  • Idris does not care.
  • Mesha thinks The Gilded is a stranger with unknown patronage from outside the Aelorian Territories entirely.
  • Kellan has no theory. She has only met The Gilded twice.

Design note (DM only): The Gilded’s identity is deliberately unspecified. Pick when the campaign needs it. Strong candidates: (1) Elran Bosk / The Chair alive; (2) an entirely new figure — perhaps a wealthy patron using the network as a tool; (3) Vaeloran himself (would explain why the network is being used to build instability so effectively — but this is the biggest reveal available, save for a truly climactic moment). Do not commit until the story needs a commitment.

Cross-cell coordination

Sending stones

Every Territorial Veilmaster carries a single sending stone paired to The Gilded. The stones are dwarven-crafted, hex-cut, worn on a leather thong under clothing. Each is uniquely attuned to The Gilded’s matching set — messages travel Veilmaster ↔ Gilded only, in either direction, once per day per stone (using the sending spell mechanic).

Second stone (rare). When a specific situation requires two Veilmasters to speak directly, The Gilded may issue a second, temporary stone — usually delivered by trusted courier — that pairs the two Veilmasters directly for the duration of the operation. When the crisis ends, the stones are returned to The Gilded. In four years there have been three such issuances: Merric ↔ Wenzel during a smuggling operation, Berine ↔ Mesha during a maritime chase, and Merric ↔ Idris during a tax investigation. All routine cross-Veilmaster communication goes through The Gilded as intermediary.

  • Quarterly meetings at rotating locations. Most recently Kolt’s Depot; next scheduled at Duskmere in six weeks. Each Veilmaster attends personally. Sending stones are used to confirm identities and coordinate arrival.
  • Written correspondence. Rare. When paper is required (documents, ledgers, contracts), it moves by Mesha’s Southern Road courier network. The Veil does not use a written cypher for routine business — the sending stones make that unnecessary.
  • Cross-cell operations. Require The Gilded’s approval. The last major cross-cell operation was six years ago — a coordinated response to a Watch crackdown that would have cost the network three captains.

Cover businesses

  • Aeloria: The Pig’s Head Inn (Gerald runs the front; does not know he is Veil-adjacent); The Gilded Quill (Edrin Vale’s forgery house, in the Grand Bazaar).
  • Ironhold: Rustpocket safehouse network — access via cellars into the Old Mines (disused founding-era mining tunnels beneath Ironhold), a laundress’s shop above (Kellan’s current hiding place), and a scattering of cover roles for cell members. Deliberately geographically separated from Warehouse #14 (Coin Cipher). The Old Mines are shared infrastructure — Cipher uses their end for goods movement, Veil uses the Rustpocket end for cell movement — but the two networks avoid each other in the tunnels by convention.
  • Stonegate: the Broken Post tavern in the lower town — publicly a rough drinking house, actually Wenzel’s operating base.
  • Duskmere: a chandler’s shop in the harbour district, run by Berine’s daughter-in-law.
  • Silverbrook: no formal cover — Idris operates through family networks that would not read as a “cell” to outside investigators.
  • Southern Road: a network of small waystations and stable-cousins; nothing centralised.

Current threats

  • Vaeloran is manipulating the network through the Aurek alias without any Veilmaster knowing. Merric suspects something is wrong but has not identified what. See below.
  • Kaelith is using Merric’s tunnels for Naturus cult meetings. Merric knows. He has not shut it down because he does not know “K” = Kaelith = Vaeloran’s network.
  • Kellan is currently framed by Drake — Session 6/7 crisis in Ironhold.
  • Wenzel’s northern operations may be compromised — the “trouble at Stonegate” thread mentioned in Session 5 is possibly a corruption purge that could put her cell at risk.
  • The Gilded has been quieter than usual for the last two quarters. Some Veilmasters have noticed. Nobody has said it out loud.

The Vaeloran manipulation

Vaeloran is engineering city-wide instability through the Aurek alias, using the Veil’s tunnels, the Naturus cult, and the Coin Cipher network in parallel. The Veil provides:

  • Street-level violence and crime spikes (feeds Instability Clock).
  • Information movement (Ambimar’s captain-level network).
  • Safe infrastructure for Kaelith’s Naturus operations (Aeloria tunnels).

None of the Veilmasters know the full picture. Merric suspects something is wrong but hasn’t identified what. If Merric ever compares notes properly with Kellan, Wenzel, and Berine, patterns emerge — but they do not, currently, compare notes.

Party contact points

  • Torren is Veil. Recruited by Wenzel at Stonegate; sent south to Aeloria; now operating with the party.
  • Merric has met the party at the Pig’s Head. Neutral-cooperative.
  • Kellan will meet the party in Session 6/7 via one of several possible paths (Merric cypher recommendation, party investigation, Torren Veil sign-drops, or Ana Kest introduction).
  • Wenzel has not released Torren. If the party goes north, or if Wenzel needs a southern asset, she will reach for him.

Cross-references

  • Group: Guilded Veil Captains
  • NPC (Veilmasters): Merric Underbough · Kellan Bracewell · Wenzel “The Kite” Tosscobble
  • NPC (adjacent): Gerald · Vaeloran Duskwhisper · Kolt
  • Location: The Pig’s Head Inn · Ashgate Slums · Ironhold · Stonegate · Kolt’s Depot
  • Plot: Merric and Orin · Naturus Cult - Sister Kaelith · Gerald’s Missing Guild Member · Torren - Personal Arc · Instability Clock

title: The Stonemarked
summary: **Goliath warrior clan in the Stonemarked Mountains. Orin's tribe.**
html:
The Stonemarked

Goliath warrior clan in the Stonemarked Mountains. Orin’s tribe.

A proud people who value physical strength, endurance, and martial prowess above all else. Practice a coming-of-age trial — those who fail are cast out rather than killed.

Beliefs

  • Weakness should be cut from the tribe for its survival.
  • Mercy in battle is weakness of spirit.
  • Strength of body and will is the highest virtue.

Note for the campaign: Their belief that mercy is weakness is what got Orin exiled. It is also what Luminos sees as the beginning of wisdom. This contradiction is the heart of Orin’s faith arc.

Current Situation — URGENT

Being squeezed from two sides simultaneously. Countdown: 5 sessions. See _Stonemarked Mountains Overview for full details.

  • Naturus corruption from the Frostwood Marsh below.

title: The Watch
summary: **The unified law-enforcement and small-military body of Aeloria and the Aelorian Territories.**
html:
The Watch

The unified law-enforcement and small-military body of Aeloria and the Aelorian Territories.

Structure

A single organisation operating at two scales:

  • The Aeloria City Watch — Aeloria-city policing, gate guards, council security, civic order. Captain Merrow Dane commands. Holds the fifth seat on the Council.
  • The Territorial Watch — patrols the wider Aelorian Territories. Local commanders in Ironhold, Stonegate, Duskmere, Silverbrook, and Crimson Outpost. Sworn to the same code, paid from the same treasury, accountable to the same Council.

Local branches may be called “the Watch out of Ironhold,” “the Watch at Stonegate,” etc. — they all report up.

Membership

  • Recruits drawn from across the Territories. Hard, fair selection.
  • Two-year minimum service. Most stay longer.
  • Equipment: standard chain or studded leather, sword and shield, crossbow or longbow on rotation.
  • Watch-tabard: dark green wool with the Aeloria sigil (a four-pointed crossroads star, gold thread). Worn over armour.

What they actually do

  • In Aeloria city: patrols, gate duty, criminal investigation, Council security.
  • In the Territories: road patrols, response to local violence, escort details for caravans (rare), diplomatic escort details (when foreign dignitaries are present).

In the current campaign

Brenna Hartwell, the caravan master for Session 5, is a retired Watch sergeant. She knows the southern road well and is well-respected by current Watch officers.

Captain Merrow Dane (Council Seat 5) is “convinced, not corrupt” about Vaeloran. He’d support emergency powers because he believes Vaeloran is a stabilising force — not because he’s been bribed. This is one of the most dangerous kinds of ally for Vaeloran’s plans.

Torren is a former Watch corporal. Served eleven years at the Stonegate garrison before being publicly discharged for corruption. This is a live tripwire — see his backstory. Any Watch tabard makes him watch the exits. Any officer from Stonegate is a potential disaster if they recognise him.

The Watch escort accompanying Envoy Veris Caelthorn (Session 6) is four soldiers under a serjeant. Polite, professional. They are not under Veris’s command — they’re providing protocol-required diplomatic escort while he’s in Aelorian Territory. They can be asked about Stonegate, the Stonemarked, the southern road, and current Watch concerns.

Standing in the campaign

  • Not corrupt institutionally. Honest body. Could become a major ally to the party if they earn trust.
  • Merrow Dane’s belief in Vaeloran is the institutional weak point. If the party can shake the Captain’s certainty, the Watch tips against Vaeloran.
  • Underused as story device so far. This faction is here for future scenes — diplomatic escorts, criminal investigations, council security, manhunts.

Named Watch NPCs

Stonegate garrison (Torren’s past)

  • Captain Rikhardt Vall — commands the entire Stonegate garrison. Was Torren’s lieutenant. Signed his discharge. Live tripwire.
  • Sergeant Nell Vissen — Torren’s old comrade. Spoke up for him at the hearing. Never got over it. Potential ally if Torren handles her well.

Elsewhere in the Territories (placeholder / develop as needed)

  • Sergeant Saln — a Watch rider seen on Day 1 of Session 5 (Watch out of Ironhold, on his way north with “trouble at Stonegate” news). Brenna knows him.
  • Lieutenant Mara Volk — Ironhold Watch commander. Steady, sceptical of the Aurum Dominion’s recent overtures. Could become an ally.
  • Sergeant Briar Holm — Aeloria gate-watch under Captain Dane. Friendly to caravan masters. Useful background contact in Aeloria.

Cross-references

  • NPC: Brenna Hartwell · Aeloria Council (Merrow Dane Seat 5)
  • Faction: Aeloria Council
  • Plot: Main Plot - Vaeloran Conspiracy
